subject: Informative prior for positive only expected value

messages.author: 89753235781499cd
messages.subject: Informative prior for positive only expected value
parts:
I have been trialling a model on species counts (count data from 0-60). I want to include what I think should be an informative prior to ensure that the expected values are all positive and potentially bound at an upper limit of 60. I just can't seem to figure out where in the code I can state this or how to go about it. I am currently using pc priors see code below. Does anyone have any advise or resources I could look into? Thanks in advance

inla.setOption(scale.model.default = TRUE)

U <- 0.1
hyper.prec = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec",
                               param = c(U, 0.05)))
f<- species ~ var1 + var2 + Var3*Var4 +
  f(Var5, Var6, model = "rw2", cyclic=TRUE, hyper = hyper.prec) 

I<- inla(f, control.predictor = list(
  compute = TRUE,
  quantiles = c(0.025, 0.975)),
  control.compute = list(config = TRUE,dic = TRUE),
  family = "zeroinflatedpoisson1",
  data = dat, verbose=FALSE)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Informative prior for positive only expected value
parts:
if counts are from 0-60, then the fitted model will likely give most (but not
all) of its mass on these (data) predictions. the poisson you use will ensure
positivity.

you cannot, really, control the latent process to ensure predicted new data in
the range 0-60, unless you truncate the likelihood to only be defined in that
region (which is also doable).

I do not see why this is an issue that needs to be adressed, if it is, please
let me know some more of the details.

I would be more concerned using more sensible priors for the fixed effects,
similar to what you do for the 'rw2'

all the best
Havard
